title: Acute effects of transcranial direct currrent stimulation (tDCS) on neuropsychological and affective outcomes in older adults and with depressive disorder.
summary: Findings show that transcranial direct current stimulation may have positive effects on various aspects of cognitive performance, such as memory and concentration. Furthermore, improvements in symptoms and mood have been observed in individuals with depressive disorders. In this study, we aim to test whether a single stimulation session is effective for older adults with depression and compare the effects with those observed in healthy individuals of the same age group and in young adults.

interventions.name:
Group: Depression, Age 60+ years
Intervention: 2 tDCS sessions (20 min, 2 mA, active and sham)
Electrode placement (10-20 EEG system):
   - Anode: left DLPFC (F3)
   - Cathode: ventromedial PFC (Fpz)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Ability and willingness to consent to the study
Age: ≥ 60 years (or 18-25)
Primary clinical diagnosis of a depressive episode (ICD-10: F32.1, F32.2, F33.1, F33.2)
Exclusion criteria:
Acute suicidality (clinical impression)
Other relevant psychiatric disorders: Bipolar disorder, psychosis or schizophrenia, addiction/substance abuse
Epilepsy/previous epileptic seizures
Family history of epileptic seizures
Mild cognitive impairment
Neurodegenerative diseases
Past or present neurological disorders or head surgeries
Implants: Cochlear implant, pacemaker, deep brain stimulation, vagus nerve stimulation
Acute dermatological condition of the scalp
Pregnancy or breastfeeding
Non-German speaking
